text: The number of ways, in which 16 oranges can be distributed to four children such that each child gets at least one orange, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To distribute 16 oranges to 4 children such that each child gets atleast one orange. 

First distribute one orange to each child so that each child get atleast one. 

Now, distribute remaining ( $\mathrm{n}=12$ ) oranges to ( $\mathrm{r}=4$ ) children using beggar's method $={}^{n+r-1}C_{r-1}$

$\begin{array}{l} ={}^{12+4-1}C_{4-1}={}^{15}C_{3} \\  \\ =\dfrac{15\times 14\times 13}{3\times 2\times 1}=5\times 7\times 13=455 \end{array}$

text: Let $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}a_{k}=αn^{2}+βn$. If $a_{10}=59$ and $a_{6}=7a_{1}$, then $α+β$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $S_{n}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}a_{k}=αn^{2}+βn$

$a_{1}+a_{2}+a_{3}+a_{4}+\ldots a_{n}=αn^{2}+βn$

Since the sum $S_{n}$ is a quadratic expression in $n$ with no constant term then the sequence $a_{k}$ is in A.P (arithmetic progression).

Then $n$th term of the sequence can be found using the formula

$a_{n}=S_{n}-S_{n-1}$

$\begin{array}{l} a_{n}=αn^{2}+βn-\left [α(n-1)^{2}+β(n-1)\right ] \\ =αn^{2}+βn-\left [α\left (n^{2}-2n+1\right )+βn-β\right ] \\ =αn^{2}+βn-αn^{2}+2αn-α-βn+β \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a_{n}=β-α+2αn-(1)$

It is given that $a_{10}=59$, substitute $n=10$ in equation (1).

$a_{10}=β-α+2α(10)=59$

$\Rightarrow$ $19α+β=59-(2)$

also, $a_{6}=7a_{1}$ (given)

substitute $n=6$ and $n=1$ in equation (1).

$β-α+2α(6)=7(β-α+2α(1))$

$\Rightarrow$ $11α+β=7α+7β$

$\Rightarrow$ $4α=6β$

$\Rightarrow$ $2α=3β\Rightarrow α=\frac{3β}{2}$

Substitute $α=\frac{3β}{2}$ in equation (2)

$19\left (\frac{3β}{2}\right )+β=59$

$\Rightarrow$ $57β+2β=118$

$\Rightarrow$ $59β=118$

$\Rightarrowβ=\frac{118}{59}=2$

And $α=\frac{3β}{2}=\frac{3\times 2}{2}=3$

So, value of $α+β=3+2=5$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: If $z=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{i}{2},i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $\left (z^{201}-i\right )^{8}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{i}{2}$

Convert into Euler form $z=re^{iθ}$ where $r=|z|$ and $θ=\arg (z)=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )$ if $z=x+iy$.

$r=|z|=\sqrt{\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}}=1$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant in the complex plane,

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So,}θ=\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2}\right )=\dfrac{π}{6} \\ z=e^{i\frac{π}{6}} \end{array}$

To calculate $\left (z^{201}-i\right )^{8}=\left (\left (e^{i\frac{π}{6}}\right )^{201}-i\right )^{8}$

$=\left (e^{i\frac{201π}{6}}-i\right )^{8}$

Using De Moivre's theorem, $e^{iθ}=\cos θ+i\sin θ$

$\begin{array}{l} \left (z^{201}-i\right )^{8}=\left (\cos \left (\dfrac{201π}{6}\right )+i\sin \left (\dfrac{201π}{6}\right )-i\right )^{8} \\ =\left (\cos \left (\dfrac{67π}{2}\right )+i\sin \left (\dfrac{67π}{2}\right )-i\right )^{8} \\ =(0+i(-1)-i)^{8} \\ =(-2i)^{8}=2^{8}(i)^{8} \end{array}$

Since $i=\sqrt{-1}⟹i^{2}=-1⟹i^{4}=1⟹i^{8}=1$

$\therefore$ $\left (z^{201}-i\right )^{8}=2^{8}=256$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let $⃗{a},⃗{b},⃗{c}$ be three vectors such that $⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{c})$. If $|⃗{a}|=1,|⃗{b}|=4,|⃗{c}|=2$, and the angle between $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ is $60^{\circ }$, then $|⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}|$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that

$\begin{array}{l} ⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{c}) \\ ⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}-2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{c})=0 \\ ⃗{a}\times (⃗{b}-2⃗{c})=0 \end{array}$

This means $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}-2⃗{c}$ are parallel vectors

$\begin{array}{l} ⃗{b}-2⃗{c}=λ⃗{a} \\ \Rightarrow ⃗{b}=λ⃗{a}+2⃗{c}-(1) \end{array}$

It is given that $|⃗{a}|=1,|b|=4$ and $|⃗{c}|=2$, angle between $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c},θ=60^{\circ }$.

$|b|^{2}=|λ⃗{a}+2⃗{c}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|b|^{2}=λ^{2}|a|^{2}+4|c|^{2}+4λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})$

$\Rightarrow$ $16=λ^{2}(1)^{2}+4(2)^{2}+4λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ^{2}+4λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})=0$ .......(2)

Taking dot product with $\vec{\mathrm{c}}$ in equation (1)

$⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=(λ⃗{a}+2⃗{c})\cdot ⃗{c}$

$\Rightarrow$ $|⃗{b}||⃗{c}|\cos 60^{\circ }=λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})+2|⃗{c}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $4\times 2\times 1/2=λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})+2(2)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $4=λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})+8$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})=-4\ldots (3)$

From (2) and (3)

$λ^{2}+4(-4)=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ^{2}-16=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\pm 4$

from (3)

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=-4/λ$

if $λ=4$, then $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=-1$

if $λ=-4$, then $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=1$

$|⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}|=1$

text:
Consider two sets $\mathrm{A}=\{x\in \mathrm{Z}:|(|x-3|-3)|\leq 1\}$ and 

$\mathrm{B}=\left \{x\in \mathrm{ℝ}-\{1,2\}:\frac{(x-2)(x-4)}{x-1}\log _{e}(|x-2|)=0\right \}$. Then the number of 

onto functions $f:\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{B}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Set}A=\{x\in \mathrm{ℤ}:|(|x-3|-3)|\leq 1\} \\  \\ |(|x-3|-3)|\leq 1\{|x|\leq a\Rightarrow x\in [-a,a]\} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(|x-3|-3)\in [-1,1]$

$\Rightarrow$ $|x-3|\in [2,4]$

$\text{Using}|x|\in [α,β]\Rightarrow x\in [-β,-α]\cup [α,β]$

$x-3\in [-4,-2]\cup [2,4]$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\in [-1,1]\cup [5,7]$

Since $x\in \mathrm{ℤ}$ (integers), $x=-1,0,1,5,6,7$

So set $A=\{-1,0,1,5,6,7\}$

Set $B=\left \{x\in \mathrm{ℝ}-\{1,2\},\frac{(x-2)(x-4)}{(x-1)}\log _{e}(|x-2|)=0\right \}$

$\frac{(x-2)(x-4)}{(x-1)}\log _{e}(|x-2|)=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x-2=0\Rightarrow x=2$ but $x\neq 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $x-4=0\Rightarrow x=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\log _{e}|x-2|=0\Rightarrow |x-2|=1$

$\begin{array}{l} x-2=\pm 1\Rightarrow x=3,1\text{but}x\neq 1 \\ \text{So set}B=\{3,4\} \\ \text{Let}n(A)&n(B)\text{be number of elements in set}A\text{and}B \\ \text{respectively} \\ n(A)=6,n(B)=2 \end{array}$

Number of onto function $f:A\to B$ is

= Total function - Into function

Total function $=(n(B))^{n(A)}=2^{6}$

number of Into function can be find using inclusion-exclusion principle

Number of into function $={}^{2}C_{1}(1)^{6}$

${}^{2}C_{1}(1)^{6}=$ only one image or range left from set $B$.

Number of onto function $=2^{6}-{}^{2}C_{1}(1)^{6}$

$=64-2=62$

text:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\{0,1,2,\ldots ,9\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $(x,y)\in \mathrm{R}$ if and only if $|x-y|$ is a multiple of 3.

Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $n(\mathrm{R})=36$.

Statement II : R is an equivalence relation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\{0,1,2,\ldots 9\}$

A relation $R$ on $A$

$R=|x-y|$ is multiple of 3

$0,3,6,9$ are $3n$ type numbers

$1,4,7$ are $3n+1$ type numbers

$2,5,8$ are $3n+2$ type numbers

Case 1 : Relation $R$ is valid if $x&y$ both are $3n$ type.

$=4\times 4=16\text{pairs}$

Case 2 : Relation $R$ is valid if $x&y$ both are $3n+1$ type. $=3\times 3=9$ pairs

Case 3 : similarly relation $R$ is valid if $x&y$ both are $3n+2$ type. $=3\times 3=9$ pair

$n(R)=16+9+9=34\neq 36$

statement I is false.

A relation is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

Reflexive: For any $x\in A,|x-x|=0$. Since 0 is a multiple of $3,(x,x)\in R$.

Symmetric: If $(x,y)\in R$, then $|x-y|=3k$. Since $|y-x|=|x-y|$, then $|y-x|=3k$, so $(y,x)\in R$.

Transitive: If $|x-y|$ and $|y-z|$ are multiples of 3 , then $x-y=3k$ and $y-z=3m$.

Adding these gives $x-z=3(k+m)$, so $|x-z|$ is a multiple of 3.

Statement II is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Bag A contains 9 white and 8 black balls, while bag B contains 6 white and 4 black balls. One ball is randomly picked up from the bag B and mixed up with the balls in the bag A . Then a ball is randomly drawn from the bag A . If the probability, that the ball drawn is white, is $\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{q}},\gcd (\mathrm{p},\mathrm{q})=1$, then $\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bag A : 9 white, 8 black (Total $=17$ )

Bag B : 6 white, 4 black (Total $=10$ )

One ball is moved from Bag B to Bag A. There are two mutually exclusive events for this transfer:

Case 1 : The ball moved is white

The probability of choosing a white ball from Bag B is:

$P(W_{B})=\frac{6}{10}$

After adding this white ball to Bag A, Bag A now contains 10 white and 8 black balls ( 18 total). The probability of then drawing a white ball from Bag A is :

$P(W_{A}|W_{B})=\frac{10}{18}$

Case 2: The ball moved is black

The probability of choosing a black ball from Bag B is :

$P(B_{B})=\frac{4}{10}$

After adding this black ball to Bag A, Bag A now contains 9 white and 9 black balls ( 18 total). The probability of then drawing a white ball from Bag A is :

$P(W_{A}|B_{B})=\frac{9}{18}$

Using total probability theorem

$P(W_{A})=P(W_{B})\cdot P(W_{A}|W_{B})+P(B_{B})\cdot P(W_{A}|B_{B})$

$\RightarrowP(W_{A})=\left (\frac{6}{10}\times \frac{10}{18}\right )+\left (\frac{4}{10}\times \frac{9}{18}\right )$

$P(W_{A})=\frac{60}{180}+\frac{36}{180}=\frac{96}{180}=\frac{8}{15}$

It is given that $P(W_{A})=\frac{p}{q}$.

$\begin{array}{l} \gcd (8,15)=1 \\  \\ \text{So}p=8&q=15 \end{array}$

$p+q=8+15=23$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let PQ be a chord of the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{4}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, perpendicular to the x -axis such that OPQ is an equilateral triangle, O being the centre of the hyperbola. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is $\sqrt{3}$, then the area of the triangle OPQ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


PQ is a chord perpendicular to x -axis of hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{4}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Eccentricity,}e=\sqrt{3} \\ e=\sqrt{1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{4}}=\sqrt{3} \\ 1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{4}=3 \end{array}$

$\frac{b^{2}}{4}=2⟹b^{2}=8$

equation become $\frac{x^{2}}{4}-\frac{y^{2}}{8}=1$ - (1)

let coordinate of point $P(x_{1},y_{1})$

PQ is perpendicular to x -axis so $Q(x_{1},-y_{1})$

It is given that OPQ is equilateral triangle where O is origin

so, $\angle POQ=60^{\circ }⟹\angle POX=30^{\circ }$

$\tan 30^{\circ }=$ slope of $\mathrm{OP}=\frac{y_{1}}{x_{1}}$

$\frac{y_{1}}{x_{1}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟹y_{1}=\frac{x_{1}}{\sqrt{3}}$

Point $P(x_{1},y_{1})$ satisfy hyperbola.

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{x_{1}^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{y_{1}^{2}}{8}=1 \\ \dfrac{x_{1}^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{x_{1}^{2}}{24}=1\left \{y_{1}=\dfrac{x_{1}}{\sqrt{3}}\right \} \\ 6x_{1}^{2}-x_{1}^{2}=24 \\ x_{1}^{2}=\dfrac{24}{5} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now, area of}△OPQ=\dfrac{1}{2}\times \text{base}PQ\times \text{height}(x_{1}) \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\times 2y_{1}\times x_{1}=\dfrac{x_{1}^{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ =\dfrac{24}{5\sqrt{3}}\times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{5} \end{array}$

text: Let $\mathrm{A}(1,2)$ and $\mathrm{C}(-3,-6)$ be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus, whose sides AD and BC are parallel to the line $7x-y=14$. If $\mathrm{B}(α,β)$ and $\mathrm{D}(γ,δ)$ are the other two vertices, then $|α+β+γ+δ|$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let $A=(1,2)$ and $C=(-3,-6)$ be diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus. 

In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at a common point M..

Calculation of Midpoint $M$ :

$\begin{array}{l} M=\left (\dfrac{1+(-3)}{2},\dfrac{2+(-6)}{2}\right ) \\ M=\left (\dfrac{-2}{2},\dfrac{-4}{2}\right ) \\ M=(-1,-2) \end{array}$


[IMG]


Since $M$ is also the midpoint of the other diagonal $BD$ where $B=(α,β)$ and $D=(γ,δ)$ :

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{α+γ}{2}=-1⟹α+γ=-2 \\ \dfrac{β+δ}{2}=-2⟹β+δ=-4 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} |α+β+γ+δ|=|(α+γ)+(β+δ)| \\ |α+β+γ+δ|=|(-2)+(-4)| \\ |α+β+γ+δ|=|-6| \\ |α+β+γ+δ|=6 \end{array}$

Option (B) is correct.

text: The least value of $\left (\cos ^{2}θ-6\sin θ\cos θ+3\sin ^{2}θ+2\right )$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(θ)=\cos ^{2}θ-6\sin θ\cos θ+3\sin ^{2}θ+2 \\ f(θ)=\dfrac{1+\cos 2θ}{2}-3\sin 2θ+3\left (\dfrac{1-\cos 2θ}{2}\right )+2 \\ f(θ)=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\cos 2θ}{2}-3\sin 2θ+\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{3\cos 2θ}{2}+2 \\ f(θ)=4-\cos 2θ-3\sin 2θ \\ f(θ)=4-(\cos 2θ+3\sin 2θ) \\ \text{Let}g(θ)=\cos 2θ+3\sin 2θ \end{array}$

The expression $a\cos α+b\sin α$ has a range of $\left [-\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}},\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\right ]$.

$\begin{array}{l} -\sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}}\leq g(θ)\leq \sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}} \\ -\sqrt{10}\leq g(θ)\leq \sqrt{10} \end{array}$

For least value of $f(θ)$

$\begin{array}{l} f(θ)=4-(\max \text{value of}g(θ)) \\ f(θ)=4-\sqrt{10} \end{array}$

So, least value is $4-\sqrt{10}$

text:
Let $\frac{π}{2}<θ<π$ and $\cot θ=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$. Then the value of

$\sin \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )(\cos 8θ+\sin 8θ)+\cos \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )(\cos 8θ-\sin 8θ)$

is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sin \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )(\cos 8θ+\sin 8θ)+\cos \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )(\cos 8θ-\sin 8θ)$

= $\sin \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )\cos 8θ+\sin \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )\sin 8θ+\cos \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )\cos 8θ-\cos \left (\frac{15θ}{2}\right )\sin 8θ$

= $\left [\cos \frac{15θ}{2}\cos 8θ+\sin \frac{15θ}{2}\sin 8θ\right ]+\left [\sin \frac{15θ}{2}\cos 8θ-\cos \frac{15θ}{2}\sin 8θ\right ]$

= $\cos \left (8θ-\frac{15θ}{2}\right )+\sin \left (\frac{15θ}{2}-8θ\right )$

= $\cos \left (\frac{θ}{2}\right )+\sin \left (-\frac{θ}{2}\right )=\cos \frac{θ}{2}-\sin \frac{θ}{2}$

$\cot θ=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}},\frac{π}{2}<θ<π$ (Given)

$\cos θ=-\frac{1}{3}$

$\begin{array}{l} \cos θ=1-2\sin ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}⟹-\dfrac{1}{3}=1-2\sin ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}⟹\sin \dfrac{θ}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} \\ \cos θ=2\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}-1⟹-\dfrac{1}{3}=2\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}-1⟹\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} \end{array}$

$\therefore$ $\cos \frac{θ}{2}-\sin \frac{θ}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}}-\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} \\ =\dfrac{1-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Let $\mathrm{I}(x)=\int \frac{3dx}{(4x+6)\left (\sqrt{4x^{2}+8x+3}\right )}$ and $\mathrm{I}(0)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+20$. If 

$\mathrm{I}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{a\sqrt{2}}{b}+\mathrm{c}$, where $a,b,\mathrm{c}\in \mathrm{N},\gcd (a,b)=1$, then $a+b+c$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I(x)=\int \frac{3dx}{(4x+6)\sqrt{4x^{2}+8x+3}}=\int \frac{3dx}{2(2x+3)\sqrt{(2x+2)^{2}-1}}$

let $2x+3=\frac{1}{t}⟹2dx=-\frac{1}{t^{2}}dt⟹dx=-\frac{1}{2t^{2}}dt$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{let}2x+2=\dfrac{1}{t}-1=\dfrac{1-t}{t} \\ I(x)=\int \dfrac{3\left (-\frac{1}{2t^{2}}dt\right )}{2\left (\frac{1}{t}\right )\sqrt{\left (\frac{1-t}{t}\right )^{2}-1}}=\int \dfrac{-3dt}{4t\sqrt{\frac{1+t^{2}-2t-t^{2}}{t^{2}}}}=\int \dfrac{-3dt}{4\sqrt{1-2t}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} I(x)=-\dfrac{3}{4}\int (1-2t)^{-1/2}dt \\ I(x)=-\dfrac{3}{4}\left [\dfrac{(1-2t)^{1/2}}{(1/2)(-2)}\right ]+C=\dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{1-2t}+C \end{array}$

Substitute $t=\frac{1}{2x+3}$

$I(x)=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{1-\frac{2}{2x+3}}+C=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2x+3-2}{2x+3}}+C=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2x+1}{2x+3}}+C$

$I(0)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+20$ (Given), substitute $\mathrm{x}=0$ to find value of C.

$\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}+C=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+20⟹\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+C=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}+20⟹C=20$

$I(x)=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2x+1}{2x+3}}+20$

$\begin{array}{ll} x & =\dfrac{1}{2}\text{for}I\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right ) \\ I\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right ) & =\dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{\dfrac{1+1}{1+3}}+20=\dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{4}}+20=\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{8}+20 \end{array}$

Comparing with $\frac{a\sqrt{2}}{b}+c$ :

$\begin{array}{l} a=3,b=8,c=20 \\ a+b+c=3+8+20=31 \end{array}$

text:
If the points of intersection of the ellipses $x^{2}+2y^{2}-6x-12y+23=0$ and 

$4x^{2}+2y^{2}-20x-12y+35=0$ lie on a circle of radius $r$ and centre $(a,b)$, then the 

value of $ab+18r^{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the given ellipses be :

$\begin{array}{l} S_{1}\equiv x^{2}+2y^{2}-6x-12y+23=0 \\ S_{2}\equiv 4x^{2}+2y^{2}-20x-12y+35=0 \end{array}$

The equation of a curve passing through the intersection of these two ellipses is given by the family of curves $S_{1}+λS_{2}=0$ :

$\left (x^{2}+2y^{2}-6x-12y+23\right )+λ\left (4x^{2}+2y^{2}-20x-12y+35\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow(1+4λ)x^{2}+(2+2λ)y^{2}-(6+20λ)x-(12+12λ)y+(23+35λ)=0$

Condition for circle: coefficient of $x^{2}=$ coefficient of $y^{2}$

$1+4λ=2+2λ$

$\Rightarrow$ $2λ=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{1}{2}$

Substitute $λ=\frac{1}{2}$ :

$3x^{2}+3y^{2}-16x-18y+\frac{81}{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}+y^{2}-\frac{16}{3}x-6y+\frac{27}{2}=0$

$\begin{array}{l} 2g=-\dfrac{16}{3}⟹g=-\dfrac{8}{3} \\ 2f=-6⟹f=-3 \\ \text{Centre}(a,b)=(-g,-f)=\left (\dfrac{8}{3},3\right ) \\ a=\dfrac{8}{3},b=3 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} r^{2}=g^{2}+f^{2}-c \\ r^{2}=\left (-\dfrac{8}{3}\right )^{2}+(-3)^{2}-\dfrac{27}{2} \\ r^{2}=\dfrac{64}{9}+9-\dfrac{27}{2} \\ r^{2}=\dfrac{128+162-243}{18} \\ r^{2}=\dfrac{47}{18} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} ab+18r^{2}=\left (\dfrac{8}{3}\right )(3)+18\left (\dfrac{47}{18}\right ) \\ ab+18r^{2}=8+47=55 \end{array}$

text: Let $⃗{a}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}-2\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}},⃗{b}=2\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}},⃗{c}=λ\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $⃗{v}=⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}$. If $⃗{v}\cdot ⃗{c}=11$ and the length of the projection of $⃗{b}$ on $⃗{c}$ is $p$, then $9p^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllll} \text{Given} \\ \begin{array}{lllllll} ⃗{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k} \\ ⃗{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k} \\ ⃗{c}=λ\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k} \\ ⃗{v}=⃗{a}\times ⃗{b} \\ ⃗{v}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right | \\ ⃗{v}=\hat{i}(2-3)-\hat{j}(-1-6)+\hat{k}(1+4) \\ ⃗{v}=-\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k} \\ ⃗{v}\cdot ⃗{c}=11 \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} (-\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k})\cdot (λ\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=11 \\ -λ+7+5=11 \\ -λ+12=11 \\ λ=1 \\ ⃗{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k} \\ p=\dfrac{|⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}|}{|⃗{c}|} \\ ⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\cdot (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \\ =2+1-1=2 \\ |⃗{c}|=\sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}+1^{2}}=\sqrt{3} \\ p=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ p^{2}=\dfrac{4}{3} \\ 9p^{2}=12 \end{array}$

solution.body:
Refunctioning the given function.

$\begin{array}{llll} f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{ax+x^{2}-\sin 2x}{x} & ,x>0 \\ \frac{-ax+x^{2}+\sin 2x}{x} & ,x<0 \\ b & ,x=0 \end{array} \\ RHL=\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\left (a+x-2\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2x}\right )=a-2 \\ LHL=\lim _{x\to 0^{-}}\left (-a+x+2\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2x}\right )=-a+2 \end{array} \right.$

text: The area of the region enclosed between the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ and $x^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=4$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}+y^{2}=4⟹C_{1}(0,0),r=2 \\ x^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=4⟹C_{2}(0,2),r=2 \end{array}$

[IMG]

Intersection points:

$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}+y^{2}=x^{2}+(y-2)^{2} \\ y^{2}=y^{2}-4y+4⟹4y=4⟹y=1 \\ x^{2}+1=4⟹x^{2}=3⟹x=\pm \sqrt{3} \end{array}$

Points are $(\sqrt{3},1)$ and $(-\sqrt{3},1)$

For the region between $y=0$ and $y=2$ :

$\begin{array}{l} y_{\text{upper}}=\sqrt{4-x^{2}}\left (\text{from}x^{2}+y^{2}=4\right ) \\ y_{\text{lower}}=2-\sqrt{4-x^{2}}\left (\text{from}x^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=4\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Area}=\int\limits _{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left (y_{\text{upper}}-y_{\text{lower}}\right )dx \\ \text{Area}=\int\limits _{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left (\sqrt{4-x^{2}}-\left (2-\sqrt{4-x^{2}}\right )\right )dx \\ \text{Area}=\int\limits _{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left (2\sqrt{4-x^{2}}-2\right )dx \end{array}$

Property: $\int\limits _{-a}^{a}f(x)dx=2\int\limits _{0}^{a}f(x)dx$ (for even functions)

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Area}=2\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\left (2\sqrt{4-x^{2}}-2\right )dx \\ \text{Area}=4\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\left (\sqrt{4-x^{2}}-1\right )dx \\ \int \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}dx=\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{x}{a}\right ) \\ \text{Area}=4\left [\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4-x^{2}}+2\sin ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{x}{2}\right )-x\right ]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \\ \text{Area}=4\left [\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(1)+2\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right )-\sqrt{3}\right ] \\ \text{Area}=4\left [\dfrac{2π}{3}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right ] \\ \text{Area}=\dfrac{8π}{3}-2\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{2}{3}(4π-3\sqrt{3}) \end{array}$

text: An equilateral triangle OAB is inscribed in the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ with the vertex O at the vertex of the parabola. Then the minimum distance of the circle having $AB$ as a diameter from the origin is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
$y^{2}=4x⟹a=1$

Let $A=\left (t^{2},2t\right )$ and $B=\left (t^{2},-2t\right )$ due to symmetry.

Triangle $OAB$ is equilateral:

Slope of $OA=\tan (30^{\circ })=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\frac{2t-0}{t^{2}-0}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟹\frac{2}{t}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟹t=2\sqrt{3}$

Coordinates:

$\begin{array}{l} A=(12,4\sqrt{3}) \\ B=(12,-4\sqrt{3}) \end{array}$

Circle with diameter $AB$ :

Center $C=\left (\frac{12+12}{2},\frac{4\sqrt{3}-4\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )=(12,0)$

Radius $r=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(12-12)^{2}+(4\sqrt{3}-(-4\sqrt{3}))^{2}}=4\sqrt{3}$

Minimum distance from origin $O(0,0)$ :

$\begin{array}{l} d=|OC-r| \\ OC=\sqrt{12^{2}+0^{2}}=12 \end{array}$

$d=12-4\sqrt{3}=4(3-\sqrt{3})$

text:
The system of linear equations

$\begin{array}{l} x+y+z=6 \\ 2x+5y+az=36 \\ x+2y+3z=b \end{array}$

has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the system to have infinitely many solutions, the determinant of the coefficient matrix ( $\Delta$ ) must be zero.

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & a \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ 1(15-2a)-1(6-a)+1(4-5)=0 \\ 15-2a-6+a-1=0 \\ 8-a=0\Rightarrow a=8 \end{array}$

Now, for infinitely many solutions, $\Delta _{x}=\Delta _{y}=\Delta _{z}=0$.

Check $\Delta _{x}$ :

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \Delta _{x}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 36 & 5 & 8 \\ b & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ 6(15-16)-1(108-8b)+1(72-5b)=0 \\ 6(-1)-108+8b+72-5b=0 \\ -6-108+72+3b=0 \\ -42+3b=0\Rightarrow 3b=42\Rightarrow b=14 \\ \Delta _{y}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 2 & 36 & 8 \\ 1 & 14 & 3 \end{array}\right |=1(108-112)-6(6-8)+1(28-36)=-4+12-8=0 \\ \Delta _{z}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 & 36 \\ 1 & 2 & 14 \end{array}\right |=1(70-72)-1(28-36)+6(4-5)=-2+8-6=0 \end{array}$

If $a=8$ and $b\neq 14$, the system has no solution.

If $a=8$ and $b=14$, the system has infinitely many solutions.

If $a\neq 8$, the system has a unique solution regardless of $b$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
If the image of the point $\mathrm{P}(a,2,a)$ in the line $\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y+a}{1}=\frac{z}{1}$ is Q and the image 

of Q in the line $\frac{x-2b}{2}=\frac{y-a}{1}=\frac{z+2b}{-5}$ is P , then $a+b$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
For line 1 :

$\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y+a}{1}=\frac{z}{1}=λ$

general point $M$ on line is $(2λ,λ-a,λ)$

$\begin{array}{l} P\text{is}(a,2,a) \\ PM\leftarrow =(2λ-a,λ-a-2,λ-a) \end{array}$

since $PM$ is perpendicular to line 1 , their dot product is 0

$\begin{array}{l} PM\leftarrow \cdot (2,1,1)=0 \\ 2(2λ-a)+1(λ-a-2)+1(λ-a)=0 \\ 6λ-4a-2=0\Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{2a+1}{3} \\ \text{midpoint}M=\left (\dfrac{4a+2}{3},\dfrac{1-a}{3},\dfrac{2a+1}{3}\right ) \end{array}$

for line 2:

$\frac{x-2b}{2}=\frac{y-a}{1}=\frac{z+2b}{-5}$

since $P$ is the image of $Q$, midpoint $M$ lies on line 2

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\frac{4a+2}{3}-2b}{2}=\dfrac{\frac{1-a}{3}-a}{1}=\dfrac{\frac{2a+1}{3}+2b}{-5} \\ \dfrac{4a+2-6b}{6}=\dfrac{1-4a}{3}=\dfrac{2a+1+6b}{-15} \end{array}$

from first two parts:

$\begin{array}{l} 4a+2-6b=2(1-4a) \\ 4a+2-6b=2-8a\Rightarrow 12a=6b\Rightarrow b=2a \end{array}$

from last two parts:

$\begin{array}{l} -5(1-4a)=2a+1+6b \\ -5+20a=2a+1+6(2a) \\ 20a-5=14a+1 \\ 6a=6\Rightarrow a=1 \\ b=2(1)=2 \\ a+b=1+2=3 \end{array}$

the value of $a+b$ is 3 .

text:
If the solution curve $y=f(x)$ of the differential equation

$\left (x^{2}-4\right )y^{'}-2xy+2x\left (4-x^{2}\right )^{2}=0,x>2,$

passes through the point $(3,15)$, then the local maximum value of $f$ is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $(4-x^{2})^{2}=(x^{2}-4)^{2}$, the equation is $(x^{2}-4)y^{'}-2xy=-2x(x^{2}-4)^{2}$, i.e. for $x>2$

$\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{2x}{x^{2}-4}y=-2x\left (x^{2}-4\right )$

The integrating factor is $e^{-\int \frac{2x}{x2-4}dx}=e^{-\ln (x^{2}-4)}=\dfrac{1}{x^{2}-4}$, so

$\frac{y}{x^{2}-4}=\int -2xdx=-x^{2}+C$

The curve passes through $(3,15)$: $\dfrac{15}{5}=-9+C$, so $C=12$ and

$f(x)=\left (x^{2}-4\right )\left (12-x^{2}\right )=-x^{4}+16x^{2}-48$

$f^{'}(x)=-4x^{3}+32x=-4x\left (x^{2}-8\right )$, which for $x>2$ vanishes only at $x=2\sqrt{2}$; $f^{'}$ changes from positive to negative there, so $f$ has a local maximum at $x=2\sqrt{2}$.

$f(2\sqrt{2})=(8-4)(12-8)=16$

Hence, the answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The number of elements in the set $\mathrm{S}=\{x:x\in [0,100]$ and $\left. \int\limits _{0}^{x}t^{2}\sin (x-t)\mathrm{d}t=x^{2}\right \}$ is $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Integrating by parts, using $\int \sin (x-t)dt=\cos (x-t)$:

$\int\limits _{0}^{x}t^{2}\sin (x-t)dt=\left [t^{2}\cos (x-t)\right ]_{0}^{x}-2\int\limits _{0}^{x}t\cos (x-t)dt=x^{2}-2\int\limits _{0}^{x}t\cos (x-t)dt$

Again by parts, using $\int \cos (x-t)dt=-\sin (x-t)$:

$\int\limits _{0}^{x}t\cos (x-t)dt=[-t\sin (x-t)]_{0}^{x}+\int\limits _{0}^{x}\sin (x-t)dt=0+[\cos (x-t)]_{0}^{x}=1-\cos x$

So the integral equals $x^{2}-2+2\cos x$, and the condition becomes

$x^{2}-2+2\cos x=x^{2}\Rightarrow \cos x=1\Rightarrow x=2nπ,n\in \mathrm{ℤ}$

In $[0,100]$: $0\leq 2nπ\leq 100\Rightarrow 0\leq n\leq \dfrac{50}{π}\approx 15.9$, so $n=0,1,2,\ldots ,15$ ($x=0,2π,\ldots ,30π$, and $30π\approx 94.2$).

The set $S$ has 16 elements.

Hence, the answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Let S denote the set of 4-digit numbers $abcd$ such that $a>b>c>d$ and P denote the set of 5 -digit numbers having product of its digits equal to 20 . Then $n(\mathrm{S})+n(\mathrm{P})$ is equal to $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
for set $S$ : 4-digit numbers $abcd$ with $a>b>c>d$

digits are chosen from $\{0,1,2,\ldots ,9\}$

since order is strictly fixed, any 4 distinct digits chosen will form exactly one such number. number of ways to choose 4 digits from 10 is ${}^{10}C_{4}$

$n(S)=\frac{10\times 9\times 8\times 7}{4\times 3\times 2\times 1}=210$

for set $P$ : 5-digit numbers with product of digits $=20$

possible sets of digits (using digits 1-9):

case 1: $\{5,4,1,1,1\}$

number of arrangements $=\frac{5!}{3!}=20$

case 2: $\{5,2,2,1,1\}$

number of arrangements $=\frac{5!}{2!2!}=30$

$n(P)=20+30=50$

calculating final value.

$n(S)+n(P)=210+50=260$

the value of $n(S)+n(P)$ is 260 .

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 2 & -3 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$ and $B$ be a matrix such that $B(I-A)=I+A$. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of $\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}$ is equal to $____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Observing properties of Matrix $A$

$\begin{array}{llllllll} A & =\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 2 & -3 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \end{array}\right ] \\ A^{T} & =\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]=-A \end{array}$

Rearranging the given equation

$\begin{array}{l} B(I-A)=I+A \\ B=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1} \end{array}$

Finding $B^{T}$

$\begin{array}{ll} B^{T} & =\left [(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}\right ]^{T} \\ B^{T} & =\left ((I-A)^{-1}\right )^{T}(I+A)^{T} \\ B^{T} & =\left (I-A^{T}\right )^{-1}\left (I+A^{T}\right ) \end{array}$

Since $A^{T}=-A$ :

$\begin{array}{llllllll} B^{T} & =(I+A)^{-1}(I-A) \\ B^{T}B & =\left [(I+A)^{-1}(I-A)\right ]\cdot \left [(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}\right ] \\ B^{T}B & =(I+A)^{-1}(I+A)(I-A)(I-A)^{-1} \\ B^{T}B & =I\cdot I=I \\ B^{T}B & =\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

the sum of diagonal elements $=1+1+1=3$

The sum of the diagonal elements of $B^{T}B$ is 3 .
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift
